name: InverseBench
description: Plug-and-play diffusion priors (PnPDP) have emerged as a promising research direction for solving inverse problems. However, current studies primarily focus on natural image restoration, leaving the performance of these algorithms in scientific inverse problems largely unexplored. To address this gap, we introduce \textsc{InverseBench}, a framework that evaluates diffusion models across five distinct scientific inverse problems. These problems present unique structural challenges that differ from existing benchmarks, arising from critical scientific applications such as optical tomography, medical imaging, black hole imaging, seismology, and fluid dynamics. With \textsc{InverseBench}, we benchmark 14 inverse problem algorithms that use plug-and-play diffusion priors against strong, domain-specific baselines, offering valuable new insights into the strengths and weaknesses of existing algorithms. To facilitate further research and development, we open-source the codebase, along with datasets and pre-trained models, at https://devzhk.github.io/InverseBench/.
general_score_metric: PSNR / SSIM / NMSE (problem-dependent; reported per-task or as a composite)
reputation: Newly proposed benchmark (2025) that is gaining attention among researchers working on plug-and-play diffusion priors for scientific imaging but is not yet widely adopted outside that community.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on scientific inverse problems; metrics vary by problem (radiology, tomography, seismology, etc.). Potential risk of pretraining/data leakage from domain-specific models; some tasks use small or specialized datasets so results may not generalize across all scientific domains.
